narrator.name: The Atlas narrator
narrator.voice: warm, unhurried, curious; a documentary voice that never oversells; speaks the dance's own words (names, counts) clearly
narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language
narrator.wardrobe: in each episode the narrator wears the traditional apparel associated with the dance, reconstructed with meticulous care from the profile's costume notes and the licensed images — genuine and respectful, never a caricature; sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire is never worn (the narrator stays in neutral dress with a respectful nod in colour and fabric); the pack's visual_brief.wardrobe says which
narrator.languages: master narration in English; translations per language in episodes/i18n/<lang>/<slug>.json with the same scene structure (pipeline/translate.py); names, places and counts are never translated

instructor.rule: counts out loud; demonstrates front and back; three slow repetitions before tempo; one correction at a time

scenes.title: Cold open
narration: The Dance of the Crowded Room
This is Hand Jive. 1950s.
on_screen: Hero video — MISSING
Title card: Hand Jive · United Kingdom · 1950s

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The hand jive was invented in 1957 at The Cat's Whisker coffee bar in Soho, London, by Leon Bell.
It was documented by Ken Russell, who observed that the dance was a necessity due to the lack of floor space for foot-based dancing.
on_screen: Map: United Kingdom · Europe
Image — MISSING

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Originally a social dance for teenagers in crowded venues, it has since been used in theatrical performances, movies, and as a participatory activity in stage shows.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage: Ding Dong Daddy Hand Jive (https://archive.org/details/ding-dong-daddy-hand-jive)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance involves a sequence of hand and arm movements performed while standing or sitting.
Key movements include thigh slapping, crossing the wrists, fist pounding, hand clapping, and hitchhike gestures.
Watch for Hitchhike.
on_screen: Hero video — MISSING
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Stationary, suitable for crowded spaces
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The dance is primarily associated with 1950s rhythm and blues, specifically the Bo Diddley beat.
Notable tracks include 'Willie and the Hand Jive' by Johnny Otis and 'Born to Hand Jive' from the musical Grease.
Listen for the Drums, Guitar, Bass.
The pulse is 4/4.
The music is characterized by a driving, syncopated rhythm known as the Bo Diddley beat, which provides a steady percussive pulse for the hand movements.
on_screen: Instrument names on screen as each is mentioned
Listen later: Willie and the Hand Jive — Johnny Otis; Born to Hand Jive — Sha Na Na; Nefertiti — Miles Davis (1968)
Waveform or rhythm-pattern graphic: Bo Diddley beat (syncopated rhythm)
